page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top left with page number at top right. Main text in one column, with small figure rows and a letter signature "B" at the foot.

main_text.p: Centum igitur libræ ceræ emuntur 19 aureis, & 6 albis.
main_text.head: Probatio Aureæ Regulæ fit per inversionem.
main_text.p: Colloco tertium numerum primo loco, ac numerum Regula Detri inventum, medio, & primum numerum loco tertio: Et si per operationem Regulæ, numerus in medio supra locatus redierit, bene operatus sum.
Hic aureos in medio positos duco in albos per 26, inquiens: sexies 9 sunt 54, 4 subnoto, & ƒ mente reservo, ac pergo dicens: semel 6 sunt 6, quibus addo 5, & sunt 11, quæ subscribo.

Deinde dico bis novena sunt 18, 8 scribo, 1 mente reservo, ac progredior dicens: semel 2 sunt 2, quibus addo 1, & sunt 3. Nunc producto subjicio 6 supra in medio positra, dicens: 6 & 4 sunt 10, subnoto o, servans 1.

page.notes: Hard-to-read or doubtful: the diagram symbols in the first lines are rendered as approximations of printed signs; "ƒ" in "& ƒ mente" is a long-s-like form as printed and may be a printer's abbreviation for "s" (sed/si); "positra" in the last paragraph is a probable printing error for "posita"; the final line is cut off at the page edge ("servans 1" with a trailing mark). Figures in the diagram and the arithmetic rows were transcribed as printed and could not all be verified letter by letter. Right of the number "385" is a stray mark, not text.
